visualFindings: The right front curtain crosses the forehead, eye, cheek, and jaw, obscuring facial readability despite remaining outside the collision body.
The centre part is too wide and triangular, exposing a synthetic-looking scalp wedge.
Most strands follow nearly parallel vertical paths, so the groom reads as a procedural curtain rather than grouped human locks.
The bottom silhouette has excessive individual needle tips and lacks controlled clump-level length variation.
The hair material is uniformly dark and lacks root-to-tip roughness and value variation.
decision: Retain r1110 as the collision-safe baseline but classify the visible groom as a strict visual failure.
nextAction: Mask face-crossing curves through point radius, introduce deterministic clump-level tip staggering, preserve the zero-penetration motion envelope, and re-render front, oblique, profile, and motion views.
